gen_risks.description: Inadequate access to long-term financing for SMEs and mid-caps may hinder their ability to invest in sustainability measures.
gen_risks.mitigation: NAFIN's provision of long-term financing and technical assistance to SMEs and mid-caps, as well as the development of a sustainable finance framework.
gen_risks.evidence: Lack of access to long-term financing constrains SME capacity to invest in sustainability.

gen_risks.description: Insufficient capacity of PFIs to design, originate, appraise, and monitor green loans and sustainable finance products may limit the effectiveness of the Project.
gen_risks.mitigation: Technical assistance and capacity building for PFIs, as well as the development of a sustainable finance framework.
gen_risks.evidence: The limited availability of credible MRV systems constrains lenders' capacity to evaluate the environmental performance and credit risk of borrowers.

gen_risks.description: High dependence on fossil fuels and exposure to price volatility may hinder the competitiveness of Mexican firms.
gen_risks.mitigation: Investments in renewable energy and energy efficiency, as well as the development of a sustainable finance framework.
gen_risks.evidence: Mexico's energy system is at a crossroads: focused on improving resilience yet marked by high dependence on fossil fuels, exposure to price volatility, and persistent inefficiency.

gen_risks.description: Climate change may exacerbate operational costs, reduce productivity, and heighten financial distress for SMEs and mid-caps.
gen_risks.mitigation: Investments in climate resilience and adaptation measures, as well as the development of a sustainable finance framework.
gen_risks.evidence: Mexico faces significant climate vulnerability due to its exposure to extreme weather events such as heatwaves, droughts, hurricanes, and floods.

gen_risks.description: Inadequate environmental and social risk management may lead to negative environmental and social impacts.
gen_risks.mitigation: Implementation of environmental and social risk management procedures, as well as the development of a sustainable finance framework.
gen_risks.evidence: Environmental and Social (E&S) risk is assessed as Substantial, considering the nature of the financial instruments to be used and the structure of the operation.

gen_risks.description: Inadequate governance and oversight may hinder the effectiveness of the Project.
gen_risks.mitigation: Strong governance and oversight arrangements, including the implementation of a Project Operations Manual and regular monitoring and reporting.
gen_risks.evidence: NAFIN has a strong track record in implementing traditional, second-tier credit lines and guarantee programs for SMEs.

gen_risks.description: Inadequate financial management capacity may hinder the implementation of the Project.
gen_risks.mitigation: Implementation of financial management procedures and regular monitoring and reporting, as well as the development of a sustainable finance framework.
gen_risks.evidence: The Financial Management Assessment (FMA) reviewed the financial management (FM) arrangements of NAFIN.

gen_risks.description: Inadequate procurement capacity may hinder the implementation of the Project.
gen_risks.mitigation: Implementation of procurement procedures and regular monitoring and reporting, as well as the development of a sustainable finance framework.
gen_risks.evidence: Procurement will be carried out in accordance with the WB's Procurement Regulations for IPF Borrowers.

gen_risks.description: Inadequate stakeholder engagement and participation may hinder the effectiveness of the Project.
gen_risks.mitigation: Implementation of stakeholder engagement and participation procedures, including regular consultation and communication with stakeholders.
gen_risks.evidence: The operation will involve citizens through consultation activities with various stakeholders.

gen_risks.description: Inadequate gender considerations may hinder the effectiveness of the Project.
gen_risks.mitigation: Implementation of gender considerations, including the development of a gender action plan and regular monitoring and reporting.
gen_risks.evidence: The Project will seek to address this long-standing gender gap in access to finance by channeling a portion of project financing to women-inclusive beneficiary enterprises.

gt_risks.description: The Project channels financing to SMEs/mid-caps via NAFIN through Green Loans (GLs) and Sustainability-Linked Loans (SLLs). For GLs, E&S risk is limited (resources go to a pre-screened positive list), but SLLs operate as corporate loans, making site-specific impacts harder to trace and creating risk around traceability of environmental outcomes and possible greenwashing if sustainability targets are weak or under-monitored.
gt_risks.mitigation: NAFIN prepared an Environmental and Social Management System (ESMS) summary covering main E&S risks by key sector, disclosed at appraisal.

gt_risks.description: Introduction of new financial instruments (notably SLLs) not currently deployed in Mexico, which may lack sufficient demand, drives the technical design risk rating.
gt_risks.mitigation: Substantial TA to NAFIN, PFIs, and beneficiary enterprises (BEs) to support instrument design/deployment; GFPP grant to advance instrument design during preparation; NAFIN required to prepare and adopt a Sustainable Finance Framework (covering SLLs and GLs) acceptable to the Bank prior to effectiveness; draw on global best practices from comparable SLL facilities; Bank hands-on support during initial deployment.

gt_risks.description: The Project requires close coordination and participation of several stakeholders: different units within NAFIN, participating financial institutions (PFIs), beneficiary enterprises, and large anchor companies heading the green value chains (GVCs).
gt_risks.mitigation: Develop and deploy engagement/communication strategies pre-implementation via GFPP plus ongoing TA; establish a dedicated project implementation team within NAFIN with clear roles/responsibilities; formalize PFI participation through legal agreements defining reporting obligations and performance expectations; proactive NAFIN/WB engagement with anchor companies to encourage supplier-firm participation.

gt_risks.description: Risk that SMEs, mid-caps, and participating financial institutions may not take up the new SLL/GL products at the expected pace or scale, given evolving global sustainability policies, limited familiarity with the instruments, and possible overestimation of market demand.
gt_risks.mitigation: NAFIN business-development efforts for sustainable finance; targeted awareness and capacity-building for potential borrowers; TA to help beneficiary enterprises prepare Sustainability Plans and green investment proposals; monitor product uptake with scope to adjust instrument design/eligibility criteria, subject to Bank approval.
